claims.claim: Gregory Thaumaturgus (c. 213–c. 270); Origen's pupil; bishop of Neocaesarea in Pontus.
Gregory Thaumaturgus, also known as Gregory of Neocaesarea, was a Christian bishop of the 3rd century who lived from approximately 213 to approximately 270.
He was born in Neocaesarea in Pontus (modern Niksar, Turkey) to a wealthy pagan family and was originally named Theodore.

Gregory studied with Origen at Caesarea in Palestine for five years, probably from 233 to 238, where he was instructed in logic, physics, mathematics, ethics, philosophy, Christian faith, and biblical science.
The work was originally presented in Greek under the title Metaphrasis eis ton Ekklēsiastēn tou Solomōntos.
The work survives as part of Gregory's acknowledged writings and is included in the Ante-Nicene Fathers collection, translated by Stewart Dingwall Fordyce Salmond.
Gregory's theological writings have reached us in a very incomplete state, though his Metaphrasis of Ecclesiastes is among his surviving works.

The work matters as an early example of Christian biblical paraphrase, representing how a 3rd-century bishop adapted Scripture for his context, and it has been the subject of modern scholarly study including a 1990 critical edition with text, translation, and commentary by John Jarick.
